decisionProcess.demandMechanism: Recurring corporate group and incentive-style demand from Clio’s distributed workforce, especially recognition trips, company kickoffs, leadership gatherings and employee learning programs.
decisionProcess.summary: Moderate accessibility through named Workplace Experience and Procurement leaders, but hotel-sourcing ownership is not proven. Clio publicly documents a global Workplace Experience function, vendor and budget oversight, and event operations involving hotels and flights. Large programs may be sourced through external event-production partners; the 2025 Cancún program was handled by YellowHouse Events.
decisionProcess.notes: The public evidence supports approaching Workplace Experience first, copying or routing through Procurement for supplier-process questions, and asking whether YellowHouse Events or another agency controls destination and hotel sourcing. No TMC, preferred-hotel list or travel-management policy was found.
unknowns: The target hotel’s official website, address, brand, exact property attributes and meeting specifications were not supplied or independently verified.
It is unknown whether Clio’s hotel sourcing is centrally managed, locally discretionary, handled by Workplace Experience, Procurement, Marketing or an external event agency.
It is unknown whether Clio has a preferred hotel program, TMC, agency roster, negotiated rates or approved supplier process.
The target hotel’s ability to compete with NIZUC on luxury, privacy, resort amenities and incentive experience is unverified.
No named individual was explicitly documented as having authority to sign hotel contracts.
The target hotel is too small to host a Team Day at the documented 2026 scale as a sole property.
